problems.question_body:
# Dead Pod Recovery

## Problem Description

You are managing n serving pods, labeled from 1 to n. Some pods are connected to each other, forming a network infrastructure. Each pod can communicate directly with its connected neighbors.

Your system receives queries that either:
1. Add a new connection between two pods
2. Remove an existing connection between two pods
3. Check if two pods are in the same connected component (can reach each other through a chain of connections)

A connected component is a group of pods where every pod can reach every other pod in that group through direct or indirect connections.

You need to process these queries and determine the connectivity status of the pods after each operation.

## Input Format

The first line contains two integers `n` and `q`, where:
- `n` is the number of serving pods
- `q` is the number of queries

The next `q` lines contain queries in one of these formats:
- `1 a b` — Add a connection between pod `a` and pod `b`
- `2 a b` — Remove a connection between pod `a` and pod `b`
- `3 a b` — Check if pod `a` and pod `b` are in the same connected component

## Constraints

- 1 ≤ n ≤ 1000
- 1 ≤ q ≤ 10000
- 1 ≤ a, b ≤ n
- a ≠ b
- Query type is 1, 2, or 3

## Output Format

For each query of type 3, output `YES` if pods `a` and `b` are in the same connected component, or `NO` if they are not.

## Sample Input

```
5 7
1 1 2
1 2 3
3 1 3
3 1 4
1 3 4
3 1 4
2 2 3
```

## Sample Output

```
YES
NO
YES
```

problems.question_body:
# Cloud Data Transfer

## Problem Description

A company needs to rent exactly k computing cores each day for n days. There are multiple cloud providers available, each offering different pricing plans for renting cores.

On each day, the company receives a list of pricing options from various providers. Each pricing option specifies:
- The number of cores available
- The cost per core for that day

The company must rent exactly k cores each day from the available providers. They can split the rental across multiple providers on the same day if needed, always choosing the most cost-effective combination.

Your task is to calculate the minimum total cost to rent exactly k cores each day for all n days.

## Input Format

The first line contains two integers n and k, where:
- n is the number of days
- k is the exact number of cores needed each day

The next n lines each contain pricing information for that day. Each line starts with an integer m (the number of pricing plans available that day), followed by m pairs of integers representing (cores_available, cost_per_core).

## Constraints

- 1 ≤ n ≤ 100
- 1 ≤ k ≤ 1,000
- 1 ≤ m ≤ 100 (number of pricing plans per day)
- 1 ≤ cores_available ≤ 1,000
- 1 ≤ cost_per_core ≤ 100
- The total cores available each day is guaranteed to be at least k

## Output Format

Output a single integer representing the minimum total cost to rent exactly k cores for all n days.

## Sample Input

```
2 3
2 1 5 2 3
2 2 4 3 2
```

## Sample Output

```
15
```

Implement three functions for a website's authentication system: register, login, and logout. Users register with email, password, and location information.

Key requirements:

	• Users can only log in from allowed locations.

	• A user is blocked after 3 consecutive failed login attempts.

	• The failed attempt counter resets after a successful login.

	• A user cannot be logged in from multiple locations simultaneously.

Return appropriate messages based on the status of each operation.

The messages that should be returned according to status are shown.

	
		
			Register  
			Login  
			Logout  
		

	
	
		
			
			User1@email.com registered successfully!

			  
			
			User1@email.com is not registered!

			  
			
			User1@email.com is not logged in!

			  
		

		
			User1@email.com is already registered!  
			
			User1@email.com logged in successfully!

			  
			User1@email.com logged out successfully!  
		

		
			   
			
			User1@email.com is already logged in!

			  
			   
		

		
			   
			
			User1@email.com is already logged in from another location!

			  
			   
		

		
			   
			
			User1@email.com is blocked!

			  
			   
		

		
			   
			
			User1@email.com is not allowed to login from this location!

			  
			   
		

		
			   
			User1@email.com password is incorrect!  
			   
		

	

Example

Given the following allowed locations = ["Location1", "Location2"] and commands:

	
		
			Commands  
			Output

			User1@email.com registered successfully!  
		

		
			
			Login User1@email.com from Location1

			  
			User1@email.com logged in successfully!  
		

		
			
			Login User1@email.com from Location2

			  
			User1@email.com is already logged in from another location!  
		

		
			Login User2@email.com without registration.  
			User2@email.com is not registered!  
		

	

Function Description

	• Create the User class and implement the IUser interface.

	
		• This class should have:
		
			• a constructor which takes id, email, password, and location.

			• 
Id, Email, Password, Location, and IncorrectAttempt properties.
			
				• These properties are initialized with the passed values by the constructor.

				• 
IncorrectAttempt is initialized to 0. 

			
			

		
		

	
	

	• Create the ApplicationAuthState class and implement the IApplicationAuthState interface.
	
		• This class should have:
		
			• a constructor which
			
				• takes a list of allowed locations 

				• initializes the AllowedLocations property with the provided list

				• initializes the RegisteredUsers and UsersLoggedIn properties to new instances of List<IUser>

			
			

			• the public Register method -
			
				• The method takes a parameter user of type IUser and returns a string.

				• It verifies
				
					• that the user is not yet registered

				
				

				• If the user is not yet registered
				
					• add the user to RegisteredUsers

					• return the success message

				
				

				• If the user is already registered
				
					• return the appropriate message

				
				

			
			

			• the public Login method -
			
				• The method takes a parameter user of type IUser and returns a string.

				• It verifies 
				
					• that the provided email is registered 

					• that the user does not have too many failed login attempts

					• that the password is correct

					• that the user is not logged in already

					• that the user is from an allowed location 

				
				

				• If all tests pass
				
					• add the user to the UsersLoggedIn list

					• reset the IncorrectAttempt property to 0

					• return the success message

				
				

				• Otherwise
				
					• increment the IncorrectAttempt property (only when an incorrect password is entered)

					• return the appropriate message

				
				

			
			

			• the public Logout method -
			
				• The method takes a parameter user of type IUser and returns a string

				• It verifies
				
					• that the user is logged in

				
				

				• If the user is logged in, remove the user from the UsersLoggedIn list and return the success message.

				• If the user is not logged in, return the appropriate message.

# Image Processing

## Problem Description

You are given an n × n binary matrix representing an image. You need to perform a series of transformations on this image based on two parameters:

1. **Rotation**: Rotate the image 90 degrees clockwise a specified number of times
2. **Flip**: Flip the image horizontally (mirror across the vertical axis) if requested

You must apply these transformations in the order: first perform all rotations, then perform the flip if requested.

A binary matrix contains only 0s and 1s, where each value represents a pixel state.

## Input Format

The first line contains an integer `n`, the size of the n × n matrix.

The next `n` lines contain `n` space-separated integers (0 or 1) representing the matrix.

The next line contains an integer `r`, the number of 90-degree clockwise rotations to perform.

The final line contains an integer `f`, where `f = 1` indicates a horizontal flip should be performed, and `f = 0` indicates no flip.

## Constraints

- 1 ≤ n ≤ 100
- 0 ≤ r ≤ 4
- 0 ≤ f ≤ 1
- Matrix elements are either 0 or 1

## Output Format

Print the resulting n × n matrix after applying all transformations. Each row should be on a separate line with space-separated integers.

## Sample Input

```
2
1 0
0 1
r 2
f 0
```

## Sample Output

```
1 0
0 1
```

# MySQL: InnoDB Storage Layout Optimization

## Scenario

You are a database administrator responsible for optimizing a MySQL database using InnoDB storage engine. Your team is working on understanding the internal storage mechanisms, indexing strategies, and query optimization principles specific to InnoDB. During a code review, several team members have proposed different statements about InnoDB storage layout, clustering, and index behavior.

You need to evaluate the correctness of technical statements related to:
- Clustered index structure and primary key organization
- Secondary index pointers and leaf node contents
- Row storage format and compression
- Page structure and space utilization
- Query execution paths through different index types

Your task is to identify which statement contains incorrect or misleading information about how InnoDB organizes data internally and how queries interact with this storage structure.

## Question

Which of the following expressions or statements regarding InnoDB storage layout and indexing is NOT correct?

**A)** In InnoDB, the clustered index leaf nodes contain the complete row data, while secondary index leaf nodes contain only the index key columns plus the primary key values used for lookups.

**B)** When executing a query with a WHERE clause on a non-indexed column, InnoDB must perform a full table scan, but this is optimized by reading only the necessary pages into the buffer pool sequentially.

**C)** InnoDB stores all secondary indexes as pointer references directly to physical row addresses (RID - Record ID), allowing secondary indexes to bypass the clustered index entirely when retrieving row data.

**D)** The InnoDB page size, typically 16KB by default, determines both the minimum I/O unit and the maximum number of rows that can be stored in a single leaf node, depending on row size and compression settings.

## Scenario

Your company is maintaining a legacy Java application currently built with Ant. Due to evolving project requirements and the need for better dependency management, the development team has decided to upgrade the project to use Maven as the build tool. A music streaming platform wants to implement a ranking system that sorts songs based on user engagement metrics. Each song has a name, play count, and a liked/disliked status. Your task is to implement a function that ranks songs by popularity using the following rules:

# NodeJS: Students Filter API

## Project Overview

Implement a REST API service using Node.js and Express.js that manages and filters student records. The API should expose a `/students` endpoint capable of retrieving all students or filtering them based on query parameters. This project assesses fundamental REST API design, server setup, routing, query parameter handling, and JSON response formatting. The service should efficiently handle student data and return results in a consistent JSON format.

## Feature Requirements

1. Create an Express.js server listening on a specified port (typically 3000 or provided by environment variable)
2. Implement a GET `/students` endpoint that returns all students in JSON format when no query parameters are provided
3. Support filtering by `name` query parameter to return students matching the provided name (case-insensitive substring or exact match)
4. Support filtering by `age` query parameter to return students of a specific age
5. Support filtering by `grade` or `class` query parameter to return students in a specific grade/class
6. Support combining multiple query parameters to filter by multiple criteria simultaneously (AND logic)
7. Return results as a JSON array with consistent object structure including student properties (id, name, age, grade, etc.)
8. Return an empty array when no students match the filter criteria
9. Return appropriate HTTP status codes (200 for success, 400 for invalid requests, 404 for missing endpoints)
10. Include proper error handling and validation for query parameters
11. Provide meaningful error messages for malformed requests

## Technical Requirements

**Stack:**
- Node.js runtime
- Express.js framework
- JSON data format (no database required; use in-memory data structure or JSON file)

**Constraints:**
- Must handle at least 10+ student records
- Query parameter values should be case-insensitive where applicable
- Service must start without external dependencies beyond Express.js
- Code should follow RESTful API conventions

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- GET `/students` returns all students with HTTP 200
- GET `/students?name=John` filters and returns matching students
- GET `/students?age=20` returns students of specified age
- GET `/students?grade=A` returns students in specified grade
- GET `/students?name=John&age=20` returns students matching both criteria
- GET `/students?invalid=param` handles gracefully or ignores unknown parameters
- All responses use proper Content-Type: application/json headers
- Server starts successfully and serves requests without crashing
- Invalid query parameter values return appropriate error or empty results

# Marks Analysis

## Problem Description

You are tasked with creating a `Marksheet` class that manages student marks across two subjects: Mathematics and English. The class contains two private vectors that store marks for multiple students.

Your task is to implement a function called `getMeanNormalizedMarks()` that:
1. Calculates the total marks for each student (sum of math and English marks)
2. Finds the mean (average) of all total marks
3. Normalizes each student's total marks by subtracting the mean from their total
4. Returns a vector containing the mean-normalized marks for all students

Mean normalization is a technique where each value is adjusted by subtracting the mean of all values from it. This centers the data around zero.

## Input Format

The input consists of:
- First line: An integer `n`, the number of students
- Second line: `n` space-separated integers representing mathematics marks
- Third line: `n` space-separated integers representing English marks

## Constraints

- 1 ≤ n ≤ 100
- 0 ≤ Each mark ≤ 100
- All marks are integers

## Output Format

Print the mean-normalized marks for each student, each on a new line, rounded to 2 decimal places.

## Sample Input

```
3
45 50 55
60 65 70
```

## Sample Output

```
-20.50
-15.50
-10.50
```

## Explanation

- Student 1: Total = 45 + 60 = 105
- Student 2: Total = 50 + 65 = 115
- Student 3: Total = 55 + 70 = 125
- Mean = (105 + 115 + 125) / 3 = 115

Normalized marks:
- Student 1: 105 - 115 = -10.00
- Student 2: 115 - 115 = 0.00
- Student 3: 125 - 115 = 10.00

# React: Customer Search

## Project Overview

You are tasked with completing a React component that implements a customer search functionality. The application displays a list of customers and allows users to filter and search through them in real-time. This exercise tests your understanding of React hooks (useState, useEffect), component lifecycle, conditional rendering, and state management in a functional component architecture.

The component should fetch or utilize a predefined customer dataset, maintain search state, and dynamically update the displayed results as the user types into a search input field. The implementation should be clean, efficient, and follow React best practices for component composition.

2. Implement a search input field that allows users to filter customers by name or email
3. Update the customer list in real-time as the user types in the search field
4. Display customer information in a readable format (cards, table rows, or list items)

7. Use React hooks (useState for search state, useEffect if data fetching is required)
8. Clear or reset the search functionality if needed

**Stack:**
- React (functional components)
- JavaScript ES6+
- CSS or inline styling for presentation

**Constraints:**
- Must use React hooks (at minimum useState)
- Component must be a functional component, not a class component
- Search filtering should be efficient and responsive
- No external UI libraries required (unless specified by test cases)

**Acceptance Criteria:**

- Search filters customers correctly by name and/or email
- Component renders without console errors or warnings
- User input updates state and triggers re-renders appropriately
- Empty states are handled gracefully with user-friendly messaging
- Code follows React naming conventions and component structure best practices

# Best Three Scores

## Scenario

You are developing a scoring system for a competitive gaming platform. Players earn points throughout a tournament, and these scores are stored in an integer array. The platform needs to identify and display a player's three best performances to highlight their peak achievements.

Given the following array of scores:
```
int[] scores = {1, 3, 8, 3, 5, 6, 2, 4}
```

You need to write code that extracts and returns the three highest scores from this array. The result should be a new array containing only the three largest values.

## Question

Which of the following code snippets correctly returns an array containing the three largest scores in descending order?

**A)** 
```java
Arrays.stream(scores)
    .sorted()
    .limit(3)
    .toArray();
```

**B)**
```java
Arrays.stream(scores)
    .boxed()
    .sorted(Collections.reverseOrder())
    .limit(3)
    .mapToInt(Integer::intValue)
    .toArray();
```

**C)**
```java
Arrays.sort(scores);
int[] result = new int[3];
System.arraycopy(scores, scores.length - 3, result, 0, 3);
return result;
```

**D)**
```java
Arrays.stream(scores)
    .distinct()
    .sorted()
    .limit(3)
    .toArray();
```

## Project Overview

Complete a React Password Checker application that evaluates password strength in real-time and provides user feedback. The application must render a password input field, display strength indicators, and show validation messages based on configurable criteria. The solution must pass all provided unit tests that verify component behavior, state management, and correct strength calculation logic.

The component should update strength feedback dynamically as users type, implementing a robust validation system that checks multiple password criteria simultaneously. This assesses understanding of React hooks, conditional rendering, state management, and component lifecycle in a practical security-related context.

## Feature Requirements

1. Create a controlled password input field that captures user input and updates component state
2. Implement real-time password strength evaluation triggered on every input change
3. Display a strength indicator (visual element or text) showing one of at least four strength levels (e.g., Weak, Fair, Good, Strong)
4. Validate password against multiple criteria: minimum length (8+ characters), uppercase letters, lowercase letters, numbers, and special characters

6. Update strength level dynamically as criteria are satisfied, recalculating on each keystroke
7. Provide visual feedback (color coding or styling changes) that corresponds to strength levels

- No external password validation libraries permitted
- Component must export a named export matching test specifications

- Validation messages accurately reflect current password state

- Code follows React best practices and functional programming patterns

# Job Application Portal

## Problem Description

You are tasked with building a Job Application Portal system. The portal manages job listings and allows users to perform various operations on job postings.

You are given a `Job` class with the following structure:
- `jobId` (integer): Unique identifier for the job
- `title` (string): Title of the job position
- `company` (string): Name of the company
- `salary` (integer): Annual salary offered

Implement the following functionalities:

1. **Add Job**: Add a new job posting to the portal with its details.
2. **Remove Job**: Remove a job posting by its job ID.
3. **Fetch Job by ID**: Retrieve and display complete job details using the job ID.
4. **List All Jobs**: Display all jobs currently in the portal in the order they were added.
5. **Search by Company**: Find and list all jobs posted by a specific company.

The system should handle multiple operations sequentially and maintain the integrity of the job database throughout all operations.

## Input Format

The first line contains `Q`, the number of queries.

Each query begins with a command type (integer 1-5):
- `1 jobId title company salary`: Add a new job
- `2 jobId`: Remove a job by ID
- `3 jobId`: Fetch and display job details
- `4`: List all jobs in the portal
- `5 company`: Search for all jobs by a specific company name

## Constraints

- 1 ≤ Q ≤ 1000
- 1 ≤ jobId ≤ 10^9
- 1 ≤ salary ≤ 10^7
- 1 ≤ length of title, company ≤ 50
- Job IDs are unique
- All strings contain only alphabetic characters and spaces

## Output Format

For operation 3 (Fetch Job):
- Print the job details in the format: `jobId title company salary`
- If job ID doesn't exist, print `Job not found`

For operation 4 (List All Jobs):
- Print all jobs in order, one per line in format: `jobId title company salary`
- If no jobs exist, print `No jobs available`

For operation 5 (Search by Company):
- Print all matching jobs in format: `jobId title company salary`, one per line
- If no jobs found for the company, print `No jobs found`

For operations 1 and 2:
- No output is required

## Sample Input

```
8
1 101 SoftwareEngineer TechCorp 120000
1 102 DataAnalyst DataInc 95000
1 103 SoftwareEngineer TechCorp 125000
4
3 102
5 TechCorp
2 102
4
```

## Problem Description

FindJob is a job matching platform that connects job seekers with employers. You need to implement a database system to manage users, job postings, and job searches.

Implement a `JobDatabase` class that supports the following operations:

1. **addUser(userId, userName, interests)** - Register a new user with a unique ID, name, and a list of job interests (categories).

2. **postJob(jobId, jobTitle, category, salary)** - Post a new job with a unique ID, title, category, and salary.

3. **searchJobs(userId)** - Return all jobs whose category matches at least one of the user's interests, sorted by salary in descending order. If multiple jobs have the same salary, sort by job ID in ascending order.

4. **getUserJobs(userId)** - Return the count of matching jobs for a specific user based on their interests.

5. **deleteJob(jobId)** - Remove a job posting from the database.

6. **updateUserInterests(userId, newInterests)** - Update a user's interests with a new list of categories.

Your implementation should efficiently handle multiple users and jobs with quick lookup times.

## Input Format

The first line contains an integer Q, the number of queries.

Each query starts with a command name followed by parameters:
- `ADD_USER userId userName interest1 interest2 ... interestN`
- `POST_JOB jobId jobTitle category salary`
- `SEARCH_JOBS userId`
- `GET_USER_JOBS userId`
- `DELETE_JOB jobId`
- `UPDATE_INTERESTS userId interest1 interest2 ... interestM`

## Constraints

- 1 ≤ Q ≤ 1000
- 1 ≤ userId, jobId ≤ 10^5
- 1 ≤ salary ≤ 10^6
- userName and jobTitle lengths ≤ 50 characters
- category length ≤ 20 characters
- Each user can have 1 to 10 interests
- Each job has exactly one category

## Output Format

For `SEARCH_JOBS userId`: Output the job IDs of matching jobs, one per line, sorted by salary (descending) then by jobId (ascending). If no matches, output "No jobs found".

For `GET_USER_JOBS userId`: Output a single integer representing the count of matching jobs.

For other commands: Output "Success" if the operation completes successfully, or "User not found" / "Job not found" / "User already exists" / "Job already exists" as appropriate.

## Sample Input

```
10
ADD_USER 1 Alice engineering technology
POST_JOB 101 Engineer engineering 80000
POST_JOB 102 TechLead technology 95000
POST_JOB 103 Designer design 70000
SEARCH_JOBS 1
GET_USER_JOBS 1
UPDATE_INTERESTS 1 design technology
SEARCH_JOBS 1
DELETE_JOB 102
SEARCH_JOBS 1
GET_USER_JOBS 1
```

## Sample Output

```
Success
Success
Success
Success
Success
101
2
Success
Success
103
1
Success
1
```

# Android (Java): ToDo List

## Project Overview

Create a functional to-do list mobile application for Android that allows users to manage their daily tasks. The app must display a list of to-do items, enable users to add new tasks, mark tasks as complete, and persist data using a local database. This project evaluates fundamental Android development skills including UI design with RecyclerView, database management with Room ORM, and basic CRUD operations.

The application should provide an intuitive user interface where users can interact with their task list in real-time, with all changes automatically saved to the device's local database.

## Feature Requirements

1. Display a list of all to-do items in a scrollable RecyclerView with task title and completion status
2. Implement an "Add Task" button that opens a dialog or new screen to create a new to-do item
3. Allow users to input a task title and optional description when creating a new task
4. Enable users to mark tasks as complete/incomplete by clicking a checkbox or button on each list item
5. Implement swipe-to-delete functionality or a delete button to remove tasks from the list
6. Persist all to-do items in a Room database so data survives app restarts
7. Display empty state message when no tasks exist
8. Sort tasks to show incomplete items before completed items (or maintain insertion order)
9. Update the UI instantly when tasks are added, deleted, or marked complete
10. Implement proper error handling for database operations

## Technical Requirements

**Technology Stack:**
- Language: Java
- Platform: Android (minimum API 21)
- Database: Room Persistence Library
- UI Components: RecyclerView, FloatingActionButton, EditText, CheckBox
- Architecture: MVVM pattern recommended with LiveData for reactive updates

**Constraints:**
- Single-activity or multi-activity architecture acceptable
- Must use Room for persistent storage (no SharedPreferences for task data)
- RecyclerView must handle list display and updates efficiently
- All database operations must execute on background threads

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- App launches without crashes
- Users can successfully create, read, update, and delete tasks
- Data persists after app is closed and reopened
- UI updates reflect database changes immediately
- List displays with proper formatting and readability
- Empty state is shown when no tasks exist

problems.question_body:
This problem involves calculating the area of a triangle with different formulas.

 Pythagorean Formula  =  0.5 × B × H 

B and H are the base and height of a triangle.

 Heron's Formula  =    s ( s - a ) ( s - b ) ( s - c )   

a, b and c are sides of the triangle, and s is the semi-perimeter of the triangle given by the formula s  = (a + b + c) / 2.

Implement the classes and methods defined below.

	• A class named TriangleArea:

	
		
			
				Instance Variables  
			

			
				Name  
				Functionality  
			

			
				B  
				Stores the base of the triangle  
			

			
				H  
				Stores the height of the triangle  
			

			
				a  
				Stores the length of the first side of the triangle  
			

			
				b  
				Stores the length of the second side of the triangle  
			

			
				c  
				Stores the length of the third side of the triangle  
			

		
	
	

	• 
	
		
			
				Constructor  
			

			
				Name  
				Functionality  
			

			
				TriangleArea(int B, int H)  
				
				A parameterized constructor that initializes the instance variables with base and height.

				  
			

			
				TriangleArea(int a, int b, int c)  
				A parameterized constructor that initializes the instance variables with the lengths of sides of the triangle.  
			

		
	
	

	•  
	
		
			
				Methods  
			

			
				Name  
				Functionality  
			

			
				void getArea()  
				
				Prints the area of the triangle for both methods separated by a new line.

				  
			

		
	

	

A main method is provided in the locked portion of the editor. It parses five values. The first two values are the base and height of the triangle. The next three values are (a, b, c) sides of the triangle. 

While printing area as ans by Pythagorean formula, 2*ans should be printed.

While printing area as ans by Heron's formula, return the value square of ans (ans*ans) as the answer.

The output must be in the order of Area calculated by the Pythagorean formula and Heron's Formula separated by a new line.

Note: Areas might differ for the same triangle since the input configurations might differ while calculating area from Heron's and Pythagorean formulas. 

Constraints

	• -100 ≤ a, b, c, base, height ≤ 100

	• It is guaranteed that the value of the perimeter is even.

 DO NOT REMOVE THIS LINE-->

Input Format For Custom Testing

The first two lines contains two integers, height and base, denoting the height and base of the triangle.

The next three lines contains three integers, a, b, c, denoting the length of sides of the triangle.

 DO NOT REMOVE THIS LINE-->

Sample Case 0

Sample Input For Custom Testing

STDIN          FUNCTION
-------        ----------
1         →    height = 1, base = 3
3
2         →    a = 2, b = 2, c = 2
2
2

Sample Output

3
3

Explanation

Area by Pythagorean formula = 1.5, 2*ans = 3

Area by Herons formula = sqrt(3), ans*ans = 3

 STDIN          FUNCTION

10

3
4

problems.question_body:
A search query on Google produces appropriate options to choose from dynamically. This is possible with the help of Ajax. With Ajax, web applications can send and retrieve data from a server asynchronously without interfering with the display and behavior of the existing page.

How many of the following options search for "Elon musk" as the 2nd option in the suggestions?

Assume the XPath for the search box is stored in the variable search_xpath.

Option A:

driver.implicitly_wait(10)

search = driver.find_element(By.XPATH, search_xpath)
search.send_keys("elon musk")

options = driver.find_elements(By.XPATH, '//ul[@role="listbox"]//li')
options[1].click()

Option B:

search = WebDriverWait(driver, 10).until(
    EC.presence_of_element_located((By.XPATH, search_xpath)) 
)
search.send_keys("elon musk")

driver.find_element(By.CLASS_NAME, "erkvQe").click()

Option C:

search = driver.find_element(By.XPATH, search_xpath)
search.send_keys("elon musk")

option = driver.find_element(By.XPATH, '//ul[@role="listbox"]//li[1]')
option.click()

Option D:

search = driver.find_element(By.XPATH, search_xpath)
search.send_keys("elon musk")

option = WebDriverWait(driver, 10).until(
    EC.presence_of_element_located((By.XPATH, '//ul[@role="listbox"]//li[2]'))
)
option.click()

Option E:

search = driver.find_element(By.XPATH, search_xpath)
search.send_keys("elon musk")

option = WebDriverWait(driver, 10).until(
    EC.presence_of_element_located((By.XPATH, '//ul[@role="listbox"]//li[1]'))
)
option.click()

Option F:

search = driver.find_element(By.XPATH, search_xpath)
search.send_keys("elon musk")

options = WebDriverWait(driver, 10).until(
    EC.visibility_of_all_elements_located((By.XPATH, '//ul[@role="listbox"]//li'))
)
options[1].click()

Option G:

search = driver.find_element(By.XPATH, search_xpath)
search.send_keys("elon musk")

options = WebDriverWait(driver, 10).until(
    EC.visibility_of_all_elements_located((By.XPATH, '//ul[@role="listbox"]//li'))
)
options[2].click()

Options:
A) 1
B) 2
C) 3
D) 4

# XPath II

## Scenario / Problem Description

You are working on a Selenium test automation project where you need to select various elements from a complex web application. Your team is discussing best practices for using XPath expressions to locate elements reliably and efficiently. The technical lead asks the team to identify which statements about XPath are correct.

## Question

Which of the following statements are true about XPath?

## Options

A) XPath can traverse both up and down the DOM tree, allowing you to select parent elements using the parent:: axis

B) Absolute XPath expressions (starting with a single forward slash) are generally more reliable than relative XPath expressions because they provide a complete path from the root

C) XPath supports logical operators such as "and" and "or" to combine multiple conditions within a single predicate

D) XPath is faster than CSS selectors in Selenium and should always be your first choice for element location

E) You can use XPath functions like text(), contains(), and normalize-space() to create more flexible and robust element locators

F) XPath expressions that use wildcards (*) to match any element are less readable but equally efficient as specific tag names in terms of performance

2. Implement filter functionality by department with a dropdown or chip selection menu

3. Implement filter functionality by salary range using minimum and maximum input fields or sliders

4. Implement filter functionality by employment status (active, inactive, on-leave) with checkboxes or toggle buttons

# Test Execution

During a software testing phase, the QA team needs to verify that the application behaves as intended by comparing actual results against expected outcomes. The tester has access to multiple documents including the Software Requirements Specification (SRS), design documents, test cases, and user manuals. Different testing approaches rely on different documentation as their primary reference point. For instance, some testing methods focus on validating that all specified requirements have been met, while others examine whether the software design has been properly implemented. The choice of documentation used as a reference directly impacts the type of testing being performed and the coverage achieved.

Which type of testing is primarily concerned with verifying software correctness by comparing actual behavior against the requirements documented in the Software Requirements Specification (SRS)?

B) Requirement-based testing that ensures all specified functional and non-functional requirements are met

problems.preview: Implement a simple meeting assistant. Given a list of events representing when
problems.question_body:
# Meeting Assistant

## Problem Description

You are building a meeting assistant that needs to find the earliest time slot when all participants are available for a meeting of a specific duration.

Given a list of events representing when people are busy, find the earliest time during a business day (9 AM to 5 PM, represented as minutes 0 to 480) when all mentioned people can meet for a required duration without any conflicts.

Each event is defined by:
- A person's name
- Start time (in minutes from 9 AM)
- End time (in minutes from 9 AM)

A time slot is available for a meeting if none of the participants have a conflicting event during that entire duration.

Find and return the earliest minute when a meeting of the required duration can be scheduled. If no such slot exists, return -1.

## Input Format

The first line contains an integer `n` representing the number of events.

The next `n` lines each contain:
- A string `person` (the name of the person)
- An integer `start` (start time in minutes from 9 AM)
- An integer `end` (end time in minutes from 9 AM)

The last line contains an integer `duration` representing the required meeting duration in minutes.

## Constraints

- 1 ≤ n ≤ 1000
- 0 ≤ start < end ≤ 480
- 1 ≤ duration ≤ 480
- All person names are unique per event
- Time is represented in 24-hour format as minutes elapsed since 9 AM (0 = 9:00 AM, 480 = 5:00 PM)

## Output Format

Return a single integer representing the earliest minute (from 9 AM) when the meeting can be scheduled. If no time slot of the required duration exists before 5 PM, return -1.

## Sample Input

```
3
Alice 60 120
Bob 90 150
Charlie 200 250
60
```

## Sample Output

```
150
```

## Explanation

- Alice is busy from 60-120 minutes (10:00 AM - 11:00 AM)
- Bob is busy from 90-150 minutes (10:30 AM - 11:30 AM)
- Charlie is busy from 200-250 minutes (12:20 PM - 1:10 PM)

For a 60-minute meeting:
- Time 0-60: Available (no conflicts)
- Time 60-120: Conflicts with Alice
- Time 90-150: Conflicts with Bob
- Time 120-150: Conflicts with Bob
- Time 150-210: Available (no conflicts with anyone for the full 60 minutes)

The earliest available slot is at minute 150.

# Defect Severity Class

An online education website allows users to join courses online and pay for each course they wish to enroll in. The platform has a critical payment processing system that handles course purchases, user enrollment, and course access. A bug has been discovered where users who successfully complete payment for a course are unable to access the course materials after purchase. However, users can still browse the course catalog, add courses to their cart, and proceed to checkout without any issues. The payment is processed successfully and users receive a confirmation email, but when they attempt to access their purchased course, they receive an error message stating "Course not found." This issue affects approximately 40% of users attempting to purchase courses during peak hours.

What severity level should this defect be classified as?

A) Critical - The defect completely blocks the primary business functionality and prevents users from accessing purchased content after payment, resulting in direct revenue impact and user dissatisfaction.

B) Major - The defect impacts an important feature but has a workaround; users can contact support to gain manual access to their courses.

C) Minor - The defect only affects a small percentage of users and does not impact the overall user experience for most customers.

D) Low - The defect is a cosmetic issue that does not affect functionality; users can still complete the purchase process successfully.

# Equivalence Partitioning

## Scenario

A translation website translates English language text to European languages (targeting French, German, Spanish, and Italian). The website has a search functionality that allows users to search for translated phrases. The search function accepts user input and returns matching translations.

The development team needs to define test cases for the search functionality using equivalence partitioning principles. Various user input scenarios need to be tested, including valid searches, empty inputs, special characters, numeric values, very long strings, and inputs in non-English languages.

## Question

Which of the following sets of test cases best represents the equivalence partitions for testing the search functionality?

## Options

A) Test with "hello world", test with "HELLO WORLD", test with "hello WORLD", and test with "HeLLo WoRLd"

# AWS: S3 Bucket Cleanup

As part of maintaining the "HackerStorage" project deployed on AWS, an engineer needs to perform routine cleanup operations on an S3 bucket to manage costs and ensure data privacy compliance. The bucket contains numerous files of varying sizes, and company policy requires removing files larger than 100 KB to reduce storage expenses and maintain security standards.

## Problem Statement

You are given access to an S3 bucket named `hackerstorage-prod` containing multiple objects. Your task is to identify and delete all objects that exceed 100 KB in size without downloading them locally.

### Constraints
- You must use AWS CLI commands only
- Objects must not be downloaded to your local machine
- The operation must be performed efficiently to minimize API calls
- You should verify the deletion was successful
- Handle potential errors gracefully (e.g., access permissions, non-existent bucket)

### Requirements

1. List all objects in the S3 bucket with their sizes
2. Identify objects larger than 100 KB (102400 bytes)
3. Delete the identified objects directly from S3
4. Provide a summary of deleted objects and their sizes
5. Handle edge cases such as empty buckets or buckets with no files exceeding the threshold

### Input Format
- Bucket name: `hackerstorage-prod`
- Size threshold: 100 KB (100 * 1024 bytes)
- AWS credentials are pre-configured in your environment

### Output Format
Print the following for each deleted object:
- Object key/name
- Size in KB
- Deletion confirmation

At the end, print:
- Total number of objects deleted
- Total storage freed (in KB)

# SpringBoot(Debugging): Home API

## Project Overview

In this project, virtual data related to homes is provided for many areas. The task is to implement and debug a Spring Boot REST API that manages home information across different geographical regions. The API must handle CRUD operations for home records, return appropriate HTTP status codes, and serialize responses in the correct JSON format. This exercise focuses on understanding RESTful conventions, Spring Boot annotations, and common debugging scenarios in back-end development.

## Feature Requirements

1. Implement a GET endpoint to retrieve all homes, returning a 200 OK status with a JSON array of home objects
2. Implement a GET endpoint to retrieve a specific home by ID, returning 200 OK if found or 404 NOT FOUND if the home doesn't exist
3. Implement a POST endpoint to create a new home record, returning 201 CREATED status with the created home object
4. Implement a PUT endpoint to update an existing home by ID, returning 200 OK on successful update or 404 NOT FOUND if the home doesn't exist
5. Implement a DELETE endpoint to remove a home by ID, returning 204 NO CONTENT on success or 404 NOT FOUND if not found
6. Ensure all responses use proper JSON serialization with correct property naming conventions
7. Debug and fix common issues such as incorrect HTTP status codes, missing response bodies, or malformed JSON
8. Implement validation to ensure home data contains required fields (e.g., address, area, price)
9. Add error handling to return meaningful error messages for invalid requests
10. Filter or organize homes by area/region when requested through query parameters

- Language: Java
- Framework: Spring Boot (latest stable version)
- Build Tool: Maven or Gradle
- Database: In-memory (H2) or mock data structure
- Testing: JUnit 5 (for validation)

**Constraints:**
- Must use Spring annotations (@RestController, @GetMapping, @PostMapping, @PutMapping, @DeleteMapping, @RequestBody, @PathVariable, @ResponseStatus)
- API endpoints must follow RESTful conventions with appropriate HTTP methods and status codes
- All responses must be in JSON format
- Home model must include: id, address, area, bedrooms, bathrooms, price, and any other relevant fields
- Proper exception handling and custom error responses required

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- All endpoints respond with correct HTTP status codes (200, 201, 204, 400, 404, 500)
- Responses are valid JSON with proper field serialization
- CRUD operations work correctly without runtime exceptions
- Debugging tasks are resolved (common bugs must be identified and fixed)

# Android(Kotlin): Array filters II

## Project Overview

You are tasked with completing an Android application that displays a filtered list of employees. The app should allow users to filter employee records based on multiple parameters such as department, salary range, job title, and employment status. The application must retrieve employee data, apply filters dynamically based on user selections, and update the UI in real-time to reflect the filtered results. This exercise tests your understanding of Kotlin collections, filtering operations, event handling, and Android UI updates.

## Feature Requirements

1. Display a complete list of employee records in a RecyclerView or ListView with relevant details (name, department, salary, job title, status).

2. Implement filter controls (spinners, checkboxes, or input fields) that allow users to filter by:
   - Department (e.g., Engineering, Sales, Marketing, HR)
   - Salary range (minimum and maximum values)
   - Job title or position type
   - Employment status (e.g., Active, Inactive, On Leave)

3. Apply filters dynamically when user selections change, without requiring a separate "Apply" button (real-time filtering preferred).

4. Display the filtered result count or "No results found" message when the filter yields zero employees.

5. Support multiple simultaneous filters (e.g., filter by department AND salary range at the same time).

6. Provide a "Clear Filters" or "Reset" option to restore the full employee list.

7. Handle empty or null data gracefully with appropriate error messages or placeholder text.

## Technical Requirements

**Stack:**
- Language: Kotlin
- Platform: Android (API level 24 or higher)
- UI Components: RecyclerView, Spinner, CheckBox, EditText, Button
- Architecture: MVVM or MVP pattern recommended
- Data Storage: Mock data (hardcoded list or JSON file) or local database (Room)

**Constraints:**
- Use Kotlin's built-in filtering functions (filter(), forEach(), groupBy(), etc.)
- Implement proper separation of concerns (UI logic, business logic, data layer)
- Ensure efficient filtering operations without blocking the main thread
- All filter operations must complete within 500ms for datasets of 100+ employees

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Filters work correctly in isolation and in combination
- UI updates reflect filtered results immediately (within 200ms of user interaction)
- Code follows Kotlin idioms and Android best practices
- RecyclerView adapter notifies changes properly (notifyDataSetChanged or DiffUtil)
- App does not crash when filters yield zero results
- Clear Filters button successfully restores the original full list
- Application passes basic unit tests for filter logic

# MySQL: Window Function Nesting

## Scenario

You are working with a MySQL database containing a sales table with columns: employee_id, department, salary, and hire_date. Your team needs to write various SQL queries using window functions to analyze employee compensation patterns.

A colleague has drafted several SQL expressions to compute rankings, running totals, and nested window function operations. However, some of these expressions contain syntax errors or violate MySQL's rules regarding window functions.

## Question

Select the expression(s) that will cause a MySQL error when executed against the sales table.

---

## Options

**A)** `SELECT employee_id, salary, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY department ORDER BY salary DESC) as rank FROM sales;`

**B)** `SELECT employee_id, AVG(SUM(salary) OVER (PARTITION BY department)) OVER (ORDER BY hire_date) FROM sales;`

**C)** `SELECT employee_id, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY department ORDER BY salary) as dept_rank, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY salary DESC) as global_rank FROM sales;`

**D)** `SELECT employee_id, SUM(NTILE(4) OVER (ORDER BY salary)) OVER (PARTITION BY department) FROM sales;`

**E)** `SELECT employee_id, LAG(salary, 1, 0) OVER (ORDER BY hire_date) as prev_salary FROM sales WHERE ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY salary) > 5;`

problems.question_body:
# MySQL: Window Function Group

## Scenario

You are working with a MySQL database containing employee performance data. Your team needs to write various SQL queries using window functions to analyze salary distributions and rankings across departments.

Consider the following table structure:

```
employees
├── emp_id (INT, PRIMARY KEY)
├── name (VARCHAR)
├── department (VARCHAR)
├── salary (DECIMAL)
└── hire_date (DATE)
```

Your senior engineer has drafted several SQL expressions using window functions. However, some of these expressions contain syntax errors or violate MySQL window function rules.

## Question

Select the expression(s) that cause a MySQL error.

---

## Options

**A)** 
```sql
SELECT emp_id, salary,
       ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY department ORDER BY salary DESC) AS rank
FROM employees;
```

**B)**
```sql
SELECT emp_id, salary,
       SUM(salary) OVER (ORDER BY hire_date ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS running_total,
       department
FROM employees
ORDER BY department;
```

**C)**
```sql
SELECT emp_id, department,
       RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY department ORDER BY salary DESC) AS salary_rank,
       AVG(salary) OVER (PARTITION BY department) AS dept_avg
FROM employees
GROUP BY department;
```

**D)**
```sql
SELECT emp_id, salary,
       FIRST_VALUE(salary) OVER (ORDER BY hire_date) AS first_salary,
       LAST_VALUE(salary) OVER (ORDER BY hire_date ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING) AS last_salary
FROM employees;
```

**E)**
```sql
SELECT emp_id, salary,
       DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY department) AS rank
FROM employees
WHERE salary > (SELECT AVG(salary) FROM employees);

# Julia: Predict Hotel Cancellation

## Project Overview

StayWithUS is a leading online portal that enables consumers to book individual hotel reservations. The company has experienced a significant increase in cancellation rates over the past year, impacting revenue forecasting and resource allocation. Your task is to build a comprehensive data analysis and machine learning solution that identifies patterns in cancellation behavior and predicts which reservations are likely to be cancelled.

You will work with a historical dataset containing reservation attributes, customer demographics, booking patterns, and cancellation outcomes. The solution must include data cleaning and transformation, exploratory data analysis with visualizations, feature engineering, and a predictive model. The insights generated should help StayWithUS implement targeted retention strategies and optimize overbooking policies.

## Feature Requirements

1. **Data Loading and Exploration**
   - Load hotel reservation dataset from CSV
   - Display dataset shape, data types, and first/last rows
   - Generate summary statistics for numerical and categorical columns
   - Identify missing values and document data quality issues

2. **Data Wrangling and Cleaning**
   - Handle missing values using appropriate imputation strategies
   - Remove or flag duplicate records
   - Correct data type inconsistencies
   - Create date-based features (booking lead time, day of week, month, season)
   - Normalize or encode categorical variables as needed

3. **Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA)**
   - Generate at least 5 visualizations showing:
     - Cancellation rate distribution across key segments
     - Relationship between lead time and cancellation
     - Seasonal patterns in bookings and cancellations
     - Customer type vs. cancellation behavior
     - Correlation heatmap of key numerical features
   - Provide written insights for each visualization

4. **Feature Engineering**
   - Create derived features from raw data (e.g., total guests, booking complexity, price per night)
   - Identify and justify selection of top 10-12 features for modeling
   - Perform feature scaling/normalization where appropriate
   - Create binary target variable (cancelled/not cancelled)

5. **Predictive Modeling**
   - Implement at least two classification algorithms (e.g., Logistic Regression, Random Forest, XGBoost)
   - Split data into training (70%), validation (15%), and test (15%) sets
   - Train models and generate predictions on test set
   - Calculate performance metrics: Accuracy, Precision, Recall, F1-Score, ROC-AUC

6. **Model Evaluation and Comparison**
   - Compare model performance across all metrics
   - Generate confusion matrices for each model
   - Create ROC curves and precision-recall curves
   - Document which model performs best and why
   - Provide feature importance analysis for top-performing model

7. **Business Insights Report**
   - Identify top 5 predictors of cancellation
   - Recommend actionable strategies based on model findings
   - Estimate potential revenue impact of targeted interventions
   - Suggest implementation approach for real-time prediction

## Technical Requirements

**Stack:**
- Language: Julia or Python (Julia preferred for compliance with assessment name)
- Data Processing: DataFrames.jl / pandas
- Visualization: Plots.jl, StatsPlots.jl / matplotlib, seaborn
- Machine Learning: MLJ.jl, ScikitLearn.jl / scikit-learn, xgboost
- Jupyter Notebook or equivalent interactive environment

**Dataset Specifications:**
- Minimum 10,000 reservation records

# Julia: Predict Passenger Count

## Project Overview

You are given a dataset containing monthly passenger counts for an airline spanning several years. Your task is to build a time series forecasting model to predict future passenger counts and visualize the results. This project assesses your ability to wrangle time series data, apply statistical modeling techniques, and communicate findings through visualization.

The dataset includes historical monthly observations of airline passenger volumes. You must clean and prepare the data, fit an appropriate time series model (such as ARIMA or exponential smoothing), generate predictions for a specified forecast period, and produce visualizations that demonstrate model performance and future predictions.

This is an end-to-end data science workflow, requiring you to move from raw data exploration through model evaluation to final deliverables.

## Feature Requirements

1. Load and explore the passenger count dataset, identifying its structure, date range, and any missing values
2. Perform data wrangling to ensure the time series is properly formatted with sequential dates and numeric passenger counts
3. Visualize the historical passenger count data with appropriate time series plots
4. Decompose the time series to identify trend, seasonality, and residual components
5. Conduct stationarity testing (e.g., Augmented Dickey-Fuller test) to determine data preprocessing needs
6. Build and fit a time series forecasting model using Statsmodels (ARIMA or similar approach)
7. Generate point predictions and confidence intervals for a specified forecast horizon (e.g., next 12 months)
8. Evaluate model performance using metrics such as MAE, RMSE, or AIC/BIC
9. Create visualizations comparing historical data, training fit, and future predictions with confidence bands
10. Export predictions in the specified format (CSV or JSON) with timestamps and predicted values

## Technical Requirements

**Stack:**
- Language: Python
- Libraries: Pandas (data wrangling), Matplotlib/Seaborn (visualization), Statsmodels (time series modeling), NumPy (numerical operations)
- Optional: Scikit-learn for additional metrics

**Constraints:**
- Time series data must be treated as sequential with proper datetime indexing
- Model must be trained on historical data without leaking future information
- Forecast period must be clearly defined (e.g., next 12 or 24 months)
- Predictions must include both point estimates and confidence intervals (95% recommended)

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Data loading and exploration notebook demonstrates understanding of dataset structure
- All missing values are handled with documented reasoning
- Time series decomposition is visualized and interpreted
- Stationarity test results are documented with transformation steps if needed
- Model selection is justified with diagnostic plots (ACF/PACF, residual analysis)
- Forecast visualization clearly distinguishes historical, fitted, and predicted periods
- Predictions are exported in requested format with proper date indexing
- Code is well-commented and follows PEP 8 style guidelines
- Submission includes a brief summary explaining model choice and forecast interpretation

They approach every patient and set up sessions to make them aware of this procedure, but it is expensive.

They have collected data from various hospitals and thousands of patients they approached. Using machine learning, build a model to predict if a patient will try their procedure and analyze what factors affect it.  

Files

	• test.csv

	• sample_submission.csv

Schema

	
		
		
	
	
		
			
			Column Name

			  
			
			Description

			  
		

		
			
			patient_id

			  
			
			Unique identifier of a patient

			  
		

		
			
			gender

			  
			
			Patient gender

			  
		

		
			
			age

			time_in_hospital

			num_lab_procedures

			num_medications

Problem

Perform an analysis to determine how different features are related to the target variable i.e. opted. Build a machine learning model that can predict whether the patient will opt for the procedure.

For each record in the test set (test.csv), predict the value of the opted variable. Submit a CSV file with a header row plus each of the test entries on its own line. The file (submissions.csv) should have exactly 2 columns:

Evaluation Metric

The evaluation metric is Accuracy.

Accuracy = number of correct predictions/total number of predictions

As part of maintaining an AWS project, an engineer needs to back up the existing S3 bucket to ensure data durability and disaster recovery. You are tasked with creating a backup solution using AWS S3 and the AWS CLI.

## Problem

You have an existing S3 bucket named `source-bucket` that contains important project files. Your task is to:

1. Create a new S3 bucket named `source-bucket-backup` in the same region
2. Copy all objects from the `source-bucket` to the `source-bucket-backup` bucket
3. Verify that all objects have been successfully copied

## Requirements

- Use AWS CLI commands to complete all tasks
- The backup bucket must be created in the same AWS region as the source bucket
- All files and folder structures from the source bucket must be replicated in the backup bucket
- Ensure proper error handling and confirmation of successful operations

## Constraints

- You have appropriate AWS credentials configured
- Both buckets must follow standard S3 naming conventions
- The source bucket already exists and contains multiple objects

## Output

Provide the AWS CLI commands needed to:
1. Create the backup bucket
2. Sync the contents from source to backup bucket
3. List the contents of both buckets to verify the backup was successful

problems.question_body:
# Julia: Predict Loan Defaults

## Project Overview

You are tasked with building a loan default prediction system that analyzes historical loan data to identify applicants at risk of defaulting. This project requires you to perform data wrangling on a raw dataset, conduct exploratory data analysis with visualizations, engineer relevant features, and develop a machine learning model that predicts loan default probability. The system should provide insights into which factors most strongly influence default risk and allow stakeholders to make informed lending decisions.

You will work with a loan dataset containing applicant demographics, financial information, loan characteristics, and historical repayment behavior. Your deliverables include a cleaned dataset, exploratory visualizations, a trained predictive model, and an analysis of feature importance to understand model behavior.

## Feature Requirements

1. Data Loading and Exploration
   - Load loan dataset from CSV format
   - Display basic statistics (shape, data types, missing values, summary statistics)
   - Identify target variable (loan default status) and feature columns

2. Data Wrangling and Cleaning
   - Handle missing values using appropriate imputation strategies
   - Remove or treat outliers in numerical features
   - Encode categorical variables (one-hot encoding or label encoding as needed)
   - Handle class imbalance if target variable is skewed

3. Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA)
   - Generate distribution plots for key numerical features
   - Create correlation heatmap showing relationships between features and default
   - Visualize categorical feature distributions relative to loan default status
   - Identify and document patterns, trends, and anomalies in the data

4. Feature Engineering
   - Create derived features from existing columns (e.g., debt-to-income ratio, loan-to-value)
   - Select relevant features using correlation analysis or domain knowledge
   - Scale/normalize numerical features for model training

5. Model Development
   - Split data into training and testing sets (stratified split recommended)
   - Train a classification model (Logistic Regression, Random Forest, or Gradient Boosting)
   - Evaluate model performance using multiple metrics (accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, ROC-AUC)
   - Tune hyperparameters to optimize model performance

6. Feature Importance Analysis
   - Extract and visualize feature importance scores from the trained model
   - Rank features by their impact on loan default predictions
   - Provide interpretable insights on which factors drive default risk

7. Predictions and Results
   - Generate default probability predictions for test set
   - Create confusion matrix and classification report
   - Output prediction results with confidence scores
   - Provide recommendations based on model insights

## Technical Requirements

**Stack:**
- Language: Julia (primary) or Python (acceptable alternative)
- Data manipulation: DataFrames.jl or Pandas
- Visualization: Plots.jl, StatsPlots.jl, or Matplotlib/Seaborn
- Machine Learning: MLJ.jl, ScikitLearn.jl, or Scikit-learn
- Statistical Analysis: StatsBase.jl or SciPy/NumPy

**Constraints:**
- Handle datasets with 1,000-50,000 records and 10-30 features
- Model training must complete in reasonable time (<5 minutes)
- Missing values should not exceed 40% in any feature
- Target variable should be binary (default/no default)

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Data wrangling reduces missing values to <5% of dataset
- At least 5 exploratory visualizations included with clear labels and titles

# Julia: Predict Real Estate Prices

## Project Overview

You are tasked with building a predictive model to estimate real estate prices based on property features. This full-stack project requires you to wrangle raw housing data, perform exploratory data analysis with visualizations, build a machine learning model, and create an interactive interface for predictions.

The dataset contains information about properties including location, size, age, amenities, and historical price data. Your solution must clean and prepare this data, identify key price drivers through statistical analysis and visualization, train a regression model, and provide a user-friendly interface where stakeholders can input property features and receive price predictions with confidence intervals.

This assessment evaluates your ability to handle real-world messy data, communicate insights visually, implement machine learning workflows, and bridge data science with practical application through a functional UI.

## Feature Requirements

1. **Data Loading & Wrangling**
   - Load housing dataset (CSV format with missing values, outliers, mixed data types)
   - Handle missing values with appropriate strategies (imputation, removal, or domain logic)
   - Detect and treat outliers using statistical methods (IQR, z-score)
   - Engineer new features (price per square foot, property age, neighborhood density)
   - Normalize/scale numerical features appropriately

2. **Exploratory Data Analysis & Visualization**
   - Generate distribution plots for key variables (price, square footage, bedrooms)
   - Create correlation heatmap showing relationships between features and target price
   - Build scatter plots with trend lines for top price predictors
   - Generate box plots to show price variation by categorical features (neighborhood, property type)
   - Produce statistical summary reports (mean, median, std deviation, quartiles)

3. **Feature Selection & Analysis**
   - Identify and rank features by importance (correlation, permutation importance, SHAP values)
   - Remove highly collinear features to reduce multicollinearity
   - Document which features most strongly influence price predictions
   - Provide interpretation of feature impacts (e.g., "each additional bedroom adds ~$X to price")

4. **Model Development**
   - Split data into training/validation/test sets (70/15/15 or similar ratio)
   - Train at least two regression models (Linear Regression, Random Forest, Gradient Boosting, Ridge/Lasso)
   - Implement cross-validation to evaluate model stability
   - Optimize hyperparameters using grid search or random search
   - Select best model based on R² score, RMSE, and MAE metrics

5. **Model Evaluation & Validation**
   - Calculate performance metrics (R², RMSE, MAE, MAPE) on test set
   - Generate residual plots to diagnose model assumptions
   - Create actual vs. predicted scatter plots
   - Perform error analysis to identify systematic biases
   - Document model limitations and assumptions

6. **Prediction Interface**
   - Build a web form or GUI allowing users to input property features
   - Accept inputs: square footage, bedrooms, bathrooms, property age, location/neighborhood, condition, parking
   - Display predicted price with confidence interval or prediction range
   - Show top 3-5 features influencing the specific prediction
   - Provide visual breakdown of how input features compare to dataset averages
   - Include prediction explanation (e.g., "This property is $X above average due to location and size")

7. **Data Visualization Dashboard**
   - Display aggregate market insights (average price by neighborhood, price trends over time)
   - Show model performance metrics and learning curves

problems.question_body:
SearchMe is an Internet giant and search engine company that earns the majority of its revenue through online advertising. Their aim is to maximize the number of clicks their advertisements generate.

Management has decided to investigate which users are more likely to click a particular advertisement. They want to analyze which factors affect this the most. This will not only help to increase the engagement but will also help in user profiling. 

Using machine learning, predict which users are likely to click a particular advertisement and explain how different features affect the prediction.

Files

	• train.csv

	• test.csv

	• sample_output.csv

Schema

-->

	
		
		
	
	
		
			
			Feature

			  
			
			Description

			  
		

	
	
		
			
			id

			  
			
			Unique consumer id

			  
		

		
			
			Daily Time Spent on Site

			  
			
			Consumer time spent on-site (in minutes)

			  
		

		
			
			Age

			  
			
			Consumer age (in years)

			  
		

		
			
			Area Income

			  
			
			Avg. Income of geographical area of consumer (in US $$)

			  
		

		
			
			Daily Internet Usage

			  
			
			Avg. minutes a day consumer is on the Internet

			  
		

		
			
			Ad Topic Line

			  
			
			The headline of the advertisement

			  
		

		
			
			gender

			  
			
			Gender of the consumer

			  
		

		
			
			Country

			  
			
			Country of consumer 

			  
		

		
			
			Timestamp

			  
			
			Timestamp at which consumer clicked on Ad or closed window (YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS)

			  
		

		
			
			Clicked

			  
			
			Whether a consumer clicked on the advertisement or not 

			(0: No ,1: Yes)

			  
		

	

Problem

Perform an analysis of the given data and find out how different features are related to Clicked. Also, on the given data, build a machine learning model that can be used to predict the Clicked variable. 

For each record in the test set (test.csv), predict the value of the Clicked variable (0/1). Submit a CSV file with test entries, plus a header row. The file (submissions.csv) should have exactly 2 columns:

	• id

	• Clicked (contains 0 or 1)

Deliverables

	• Well commented Jupyter notebook

	• submissions.csv

Experiment with the data, make visualizations and generate new features if required. Make appropriate plots, annotate the notebook with markdowns, and explain necessary inferences. A person should be able to read the notebook and understand the steps taken and the reasoning behind them. The solution will be graded on the basis of the usage of effective visualizations to convey the analysis and the modeling process.

Evaluation Metric

Accuracy

Accuracy = Number of Correct Predictions/Total number of Predictions

problems.question_body:
# React: Pagination

## Project Overview

Build a React application that displays a paginated table of countries and their capitals. The application must allow users to navigate through pages of data and control how many rows are displayed per page. This project tests fundamental React concepts including component composition, state management, event handling, and list rendering with pagination logic.

The application should fetch or use a predefined dataset of countries and capitals, then present this data in a clean, interactive table interface. Users should be able to move between pages using navigation controls and adjust the number of items displayed per page using a dropdown or selector.

## Feature Requirements

1. Display a table showing a list of countries and their corresponding capitals
2. Implement pagination controls that allow users to navigate to previous and next pages
3. Display current page information (e.g., "Page 1 of 5")
4. Include a rows-per-page selector that allows users to choose how many items display (e.g., 5, 10, 15, 20)
5. Update the table data when the user changes pages or adjusts rows per page
6. Disable navigation buttons appropriately (disable "Previous" on first page, disable "Next" on last page)
7. Recalculate total pages when rows per page selection changes
8. Display a message or handle the case when no data is available
9. Highlight or indicate the current page number in the pagination controls

## Technical Requirements

**Stack:**
- React (functional components with hooks recommended)
- JavaScript ES6+
- CSS or CSS-in-JS for styling

**Constraints:**
- Must use React hooks (useState) for state management
- Pagination logic must be calculated on the client-side
- Component must be reusable and accept data as props
- No external pagination libraries required

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Table correctly displays paginated data based on current page and rows per page
- Page navigation works smoothly without errors
- Rows per page selector updates display without losing user context
- All buttons are appropriately enabled/disabled based on pagination state
- Application handles edge cases (empty datasets, single page of data)
- Code is clean, readable, and follows React best practices
- Styling makes the pagination interface intuitive and user-friendly

# R: Predict Hotel Availability

## Project Overview

You are tasked with building a predictive model to forecast hotel room availability based on historical booking and operational data. This project simulates a real-world business scenario where hotel management needs to optimize inventory planning and dynamic pricing strategies.

You will receive a dataset containing hotel booking information with features such as lead time, booking channel, customer type, seasonality indicators, and historical occupancy patterns. Your objective is to:

1. Explore and understand the data structure and distributions
2. Perform necessary data cleaning and feature engineering
3. Build a predictive model to classify availability status (Available/Unavailable) or predict occupancy rates
4. Validate model performance using appropriate metrics
5. Generate predictions on a test dataset in the required format
6. Create visualizations that communicate key insights to stakeholders

## Feature Requirements

1. **Data Loading and Exploration**
   - Load training and test datasets from provided CSV files
   - Generate summary statistics and data shape information
   - Identify data types, missing values, and outliers
   - Document data quality issues

2. **Data Wrangling**
   - Handle missing values using appropriate imputation strategies
   - Remove or flag duplicate records
   - Encode categorical variables (one-hot encoding, label encoding, or target encoding)
   - Normalize or scale numerical features as needed
   - Create derived features from temporal data (day of week, month, season, lead time buckets)

3. **Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA)**
   - Generate distribution plots for key numerical features
   - Create contingency tables for categorical variables against target variable
   - Analyze correlations between features and availability/occupancy
   - Identify patterns by booking channel, customer segment, and seasonality
   - Document findings in narrative or visual format

4. **Feature Engineering**
   - Create interaction features (e.g., lead time × season, booking channel × customer type)
   - Develop aggregated features (e.g., rolling averages of occupancy, historical availability rates)
   - Extract temporal features from dates (day of week, holidays, peak seasons)
   - Apply domain knowledge to select predictive features

5. **Model Development**
   - Split data into training and validation sets (appropriate ratio, e.g., 80/20)
   - Train at least two different model types (e.g., logistic regression, decision tree, random forest, gradient boosting)
   - Perform hyperparameter tuning using cross-validation or grid search
   - Evaluate models using appropriate metrics (accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, AUC-ROC for classification; RMSE, MAE for regression)
   - Select the best-performing model

6. **Model Validation and Interpretation**
   - Generate confusion matrix and classification report
   - Create ROC curve or other performance visualization
   - Identify feature importance scores
   - Validate assumptions and model limitations

7. **Prediction Generation**
   - Apply final model to test dataset
   - Generate predictions with confidence scores or probabilities
   - Output predictions in specified CSV format with required columns

8. **Data Visualization**
   - Confusion matrix heatmap
   - Feature importance bar chart
   - ROC curve or lift chart
   - Time series plots of availability patterns
   - Distribution comparisons (train vs. test)
   - Business-focused visualizations (availability by channel, seasonality patterns)

## Technical Requirements

**Technology Stack:**
- Language: R
- Required packages: tidyverse (ggplot2, dplyr), caret, rpart, random

problems.question_body:
# React: Search and Sort Books

## Project Overview

You are tasked with completing a React component that implements a dynamic book management interface. The application displays a collection of books and allows users to filter results by search term and sort by genre. This exercise tests your understanding of React hooks (useState, useEffect), component state management, props handling, and array manipulation methods. The component must efficiently handle user interactions and update the displayed list in real-time as filters are applied.

## Feature Requirements

1. Display a list of books with title, author, genre, and publication year
2. Implement a search input field that filters books by title or author name (case-insensitive, partial matching)
3. Implement a genre dropdown/select menu that filters books by their assigned genre
4. Implement a sort dropdown that allows sorting by title (A-Z), author (A-Z), or year (newest first)
5. Combine multiple filters so search and genre selection work together
6. Display the count of filtered results
7. Show a "No books found" message when filters return zero results
8. Reset all filters with a "Clear Filters" button that clears search input and resets dropdown selections to default
9. Ensure the component updates immediately as users type or change selections (debouncing optional but recommended for search)

## Technical Requirements

**Stack:**
- React 16.8+ (hooks-based functional components)
- JavaScript ES6+
- CSS (or CSS-in-JS for styling)

**Constraints:**
- Must use React hooks (useState minimum, useEffect optional)
- Component must accept a `books` prop containing an array of book objects with properties: id, title, author, genre, year
- All filtering and sorting must occur on the client-side
- Search should be case-insensitive
- Genre filter should display unique genres from the books array

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- All 9 features listed above function correctly
- Code is clean, readable, and follows React best practices
- Component re-renders only when necessary
- No console errors or warnings
- UI is responsive and user-friendly
- Filter combinations produce correct results (e.g., search "Harry" + genre "Fantasy" returns only matching results)
- Sample data provided includes at least 10 books across 3+ genres

problems.preview: A business has the following setup in Salesforce.
problems.question_body:
A business has the following setup in Salesforce.

	• On the Account object, there is a custom picklist field with the name Customer_Type__c with two possible values:

	
		• New

		• Existing

	
	

	• There are two Price Books in Salesforce.
	
		• New Customer Price

		• Existing Customer Price

	
	

	• All of the Products are available in both Price Books with different prices set by the business.

	• As per the business process, it is required that the Account Type as New should be provided the Products with the price mentioned in the New Customer Price Price Book, and the Account Type as Existing should be provided the Products with the price in the Existing Customer Price price book.

The business requirement is to be able to select only applicable product prices while adding products into the Opportunity Product records from the standard Opportunity page Add Products button.

How can this be achieved?

Options (choose all that apply):
A) Create 2 Opportunity record types: New and Existing to handle 2 different custom types.
B) Override the "Add Products" button on Opportunity to open up a custom page that can provide the Products option as per the Account "Customer_Type__c" field value.
C) A flow on Account object to update Price Book on Opportunity based on Account "Customer_Type__c" field.
D) A Trigger on Opportunity object to update Price Book based on Account "Customer_Type__c" field.
E) Using automation, create cloned products under the Account record as per the Account "Customer_Type__c" field value.
